draft.title: Technological, geographic and institutional influences
card: New technology can change what a business sells and how it works. Online sales and automated machines are examples.
Location, climate and distance affect costs and customers. A remote business pays more to move goods, and weather can change demand or supply.

Institutions are organisations that set or enforce rules. The ATO (Australian Taxation Office) administers tax. The ACCC (Australian Competition and Consumer Commission) enforces consumer and competition law.
A business cannot control these forces, so it must adapt. These influences sit in the external environment.
draft.remember: Technology changes how, geography changes where and what it costs, institutions set the rules.

a.q: Which of these is an example of an institutional influence on a business?
opts: The ACCC investigating a firm for misleading advertising
A rival opening a shop on the same street
A supplier raising its prices for timber
A drought reducing local farm output
a.why: The ACCC is an institution that enforces rules businesses must follow. A rival and a supplier are part of the market, and a drought is a geographic influence, so none of those is institutional.
a.clue: Look for an organisation that enforces rules.

b.q: Ben runs a bakery in a remote town in Western Australia. Flour is trucked in over a very long distance, so his costs are high. Which influence is this?
opts: Geographic, because distance affects his costs
Institutional, because he must follow rules
Technological, because flour is made in factories
b.why: Distance from suppliers raises his transport costs, which is a geographic influence. Trucks are involved, but the problem is the distance, not new technology changing how he works.
b.clue: What is making his costs high: a new tool, a rule, or where he is?

a.best: The ACCC investigating a firm for misleading advertising

b.best: Geographic, because distance affects his costs
